ops.title: Metal guest as relay-only services VM; host holds the model plane (Phase 6)
ops.body:
# Metal is relay-only; the host serves the models

Since the 2026-07 migration (phases 1–6), the model plane lives on the HOST (`yasyf-home`): rapid-mlx behind an idle-unload activator on tailnet-IP:8000 (`scripts/host/model-activator.py`) and mlx-audio STT on :8765. metal's `rapid-mlx`/`mlx-audio` launchd daemons are thin socat TCP relays that bind metal's own tailnet IP and forward to the host (`darwin/metal.nix`, `socatBin`); hermes keeps calling `metal:8000`/`metal:8765` unchanged. hermes is deliberately NOT repointed at the host — the relay topology keeps a compromised agent VM without any host grant (tailnet ACL: only `tag:metal → yasyf-home tcp:8000,8765`).

## Constraints that bite

- **App firewall keys on the RESOLVED binary.** nix socat's `bin/socat` is a symlink to `bin/socat1`; `socketfilterfw --add` of the symlink registers nothing and inbound is silently swallowed (handshake completes in the listen backlog, `accept()` never fires). `socatBin = "${pkgs.socat}/bin/socat1"` single-sources the exec lines and BOTH firewall loops — keep it that way.
- **Relay options are load-bearing**: `connect-timeout=10` + `max-children=64` bound child pile-up when the host is unreachable-but-in-netmap (the host activator always accepts instantly, so connect-timeout never bites cold wakes); `-t 600` covers half-closing clients (socat's default post-EOF grace is 0.5 s — kills a >0.5 s generation mid-stream).
- **Guest sizing**: 16 GB / 2 vCPU (`packer/metal.pkr.hcl` for fresh builds; the live VM was resized via `just resize-metal` → `scripts/resize-metal.sh`: `bootout_drain` → `tart set` → `write_agent` plist rewrite → kickstart). The iogpu wired-limit sysctl auto-tracks `hw.memsize` and now computes BELOW Apple's default — harmless, metal runs no GPU work.
- **Teardown is idempotent activation-time cleanup** (the omlx-retirement idiom): the phase-6 block `rm -rf`s the guest venvs and `socketfilterfw --remove`s retired entries with `|| true` on every activation. Reuse this pattern for future retirements; blocks must tolerate paths that no longer exist (the mlxaudio share is unmounted post-resize).
- **In-guest STT fallback history**: mlx-audio's own multi-threaded server crashes granite-speech ("no Stream(gpu,1) in current thread" — MLX streams are per-thread); the single-worker `darwin/stt-server.py` exists for that reason and NOW RUNS ON THE HOST (`scripts/host/mlx-audio-wrapper.sh` execs `~/.yclaw/state/mlx-audio/host-venv`). The file stays even though metal.nix no longer references it.
- **`~/.yclaw/state/mlx-audio` is the HOST's dir**: `host-venv/` is the live host STT venv; only the sibling `venv/` (the retired guest venv) was removable. Never delete the dir wholesale.
- **Metal's closure builds IN-GUEST only** (the host is nix-less after the de-Nix). And the guest's repo-share virtiofs cache pins recently-guest-read files through host-side edits: redeploy-after-edit silently deploys the stale pre-edit tree or fails loud on truncation — reboot the guest before `just redeploy metal` whenever the changed files were read by the guest this boot, then confirm "reloading service" lines + the new exec in `ps`.
ops.when: Before modifying metal's service topology, rapid-mlx/STT serving architecture, resize operations, or attempting similar multi-phase VM teardowns
